provider: Nebula Block — Standard object storage tier (storage free, egress billed)

free_tier.stated: No storage quota on the Standard tier — it is priced at $0/GB/month by design: 'Standard — Stored data: Free — Durable, high-capacity storage. The default'. The paid tiers are Performance at $0.015/GB/month and Accelerated at $0.02/GB/month. There is no published cap on bytes stored, only 'availability varies — a tier can show as out of stock'.

egress.terms: Cheaper than AWS at $0.09/GB but nowhere near free, and it inverts the usual shape — you pay to read, not to write.

tooling: Real S3: s3cmd, boto3, AWS SDKs, documented setup pages per OS and per language. A workspace issues an access key pair; buckets live inside it and are private by default, switchable to public, in which case 'objects can be accessed directly via permanent URL'. Platform API exposes usage reporting (24h/7d/30d) and key rotation, and usage is metered hourly.
chaining: Workspaces are the multiplier and nothing published caps how many you create. The genuinely interesting property is the price inversion: at $0 storage and $10/TB egress this is a very cheap place to PARK 20 TB (write-once, rare read = the cold-archive workload) and an expensive place to serve from. So the correct chain is Nebula Block as the backing store, with Cloudflare in front so the paid egress is consumed once by the cache rather than once per request.
limits_note: Credit on the account is a stated prerequisite, bought with a payment card or USDC. Tier availability varies: a tier can show as out of stock. Bucket names get a platform prefix (u-<id>-<workspace>.<bucket>), so the name the S3 tools see is read from the console. No per-object cap is published.

identity_cost.detail: email and password, or a Google account, then an activation email; object storage needs credit bought in advance with a payment card or USDC, so no card is needed when paying in USDC; one payment card cannot be added to more than one account

reliability_note: Services may be geo-restricted, and access from outside the provider's list of supported countries may result in service restrictions or account suspension.
